Lunsford: A Journey of Success and Excellence
Welcome to Lunsford Primary School
It is our aim to develop a successful partnership with you so that your child is given every possible opportunity to succeed and excel. Lunsford is a school where children’s learning is valued and their knowledge, experience, creativity, self-expression, imagination and understanding can flourish. We provide a foundation for life in a happy, safe, high achieving school, where all individuals have high expectations of themselves, respect each other and strive to excel. We are a school which the whole school community are proud to belong to and be a part of - children, staff, parents and governors.

SEND - Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator - Ms S Beckett
Contact Number 01732 843352
email via - office@lunsford.kent.sch.uk
At Lunsford Primary School, we believe that every child is unique and on their own individual learning journey. All of our teachers are teachers of children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities. Through high-quality teaching, inclusive practice and carefully tailored support, we strive to meet the needs of all learners, enabling them to flourish academically, socially and emotionally.
Our Approach to SEND
We use our best endeavours to identify and meet the needs of children with SEND through a graduated approach to support. We work closely with pupils, parents, carers and external agencies to ensure that appropriate provision is in place and that progress is carefully monitored.
SEND Provision at Lunsford
Provision is organised around the four broad areas of need identified in the SEND Code of Practice (2015):
Support is provided through a tiered approach:
Cognition and Learning
Communication and Interaction
Physical and/or Sensory Needs
Social, Emotional and Mental Health Needs
Universal Provision
High-quality, inclusive classroom teaching that meets the needs of all pupils.
Targeted Provision
Additional small-group interventions and catch-up programmes designed to address specific areas of need.
Personalised Provision
Individualised support and interventions for pupils with identified Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.
Meet Our SEND Team
Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO)
Ms Sarah Beckett oversees SEND provision across the school.
Working Days: Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday Telephone: 01732 843352
Email via: office@lunsford.kent.sch.uk
Family Liaison Officer (FLO)
If you require advice, guidance or pastoral support for your child or family, please contact:
Mrs Amy Taylor Email: ataylor@lunsford.kent.sch.uk Telephone: 01732 843352
SEND Policies and Information
Please see the documents below for further information:
Lunsford SEND Information Report 2025–2026
Mainstream Core Standards
Children and their families are at the heart of everything we do. All schools are required to make appropriate provision for children with SEND, taking account of their individual strengths and needs.
The SEND Mainstream Core Standards provides guidance for schools on how to meet the needs of children and young people with SEND, through inclusive practice, high quality teaching and appropriate support.
The SEND Mainstream Core Standards Parent Guide explains in a parent-friendly summary, how schools, local authorities and health services work together to ensure that children and young people with SEND receive the support they need. It provides a summary of the expectations and guidance given to schools across Kent.
Mainstream Core Standards Guide
Special educational needs mainstream core standards
Mainstream Core Standards - Parent Guide
Mainstream Core Standards guide for parents
These resources help ensure that schools are doing everything possible to provide effective support, remove barriers to learning and enable every child to succeed.

Children's Therapies - The Pod | Kent Community Health NHS Foundation Trust
and a free advice helpline is available:
Children's Therapies Advice Line Information

Every local authority is required to publish a SEND Local Offer, outlining the support, services and information available for children and young people with SEND and their families.

Better still, the Amazon Android app has recently been updated and you can very simply add us as your charity for AmazonSmile. Go to your account settings and select AmazonSmile. Switch the toggle to 'on' and select 'Friends Of Lunsford Primary School' from the list and confirm.
It really is a simple as that! No need to do anything else. Everytime you shop on Amazon it will donate much needed funds to FoLS to benefit everyone at Lunsford Primary School.
Ask your employer about match funding or other charitable donations. Many businesses and companies offer donations to charities, particularly as they can off-set this when it comes to their tax returns.

They also have ranges to suit all kinds of annual celebrations to ease the time spent on signing cards or personalising gift tags. Follow the link below to have a look.

Supporting Our School Community
Friends of Lunsford Primary School (FoLS) is the school's Parent Association and registered charity (Charity Number: 1174321).
All parents, carers and guardians of children attending Lunsford Primary School automatically become members of FoLS and are warmly invited to get involved.
FoLS was re-established in 2016 by a dedicated group of parent volunteers and continues to play an important role in supporting the school community. Through fundraising events, community activities and grant applications, FoLS helps to provide additional opportunities and resources that benefit all of our children.
Since 2017, funds raised by FoLS have contributed to a variety of projects and initiatives designed to enhance the school experience for pupils.
What Does FoLS Do?
FoLS works closely with the school to organise events and raise funds throughout the year. Popular events include:
As well as raising money, FoLS helps to strengthen our school community by bringing families, staff and children together.

Get Involved
FoLS is always looking for new volunteers and welcomes any support, whether you can give a little time or a lot.
Every contribution makes a difference, and there are many ways to get involved.

If you have experience with computers, spreadsheets, design or administration, your skills could be invaluable.

Sharing Ideas
Fresh ideas are always welcome.
Whether you have suggestions for new events, fundraising opportunities, community projects or prize donations, we'd love to hear from you.
Why Volunteer?
Volunteering with FoLS is a fantastic way to:
No experience is needed—just enthusiasm and a willingness to help.
Support your child's school

Remote Learning
Remote Learning and Digital Learning Support
At Lunsford Primary School, we recognise the importance of ensuring that all children can access learning opportunities, whether they are learning in school or at home.
We are committed to providing appropriate support for families who may experience barriers to accessing digital learning. If a child does not have access to an appropriate device or internet connection, parents and carers are encouraged to contact the school so that we can discuss how we can support them.
Where appropriate, we may provide access to devices or alternative learning resources to help ensure that children can continue to engage with their education.
Remote Learning Policy Lunsford 2024
Our Approach to Remote Learning
When remote learning is required, children will receive learning activities through the platforms and communication systems used by the school.
Learning will be designed to reflect our curriculum and will provide a balance of:
We aim to ensure that children continue to experience a broad and balanced curriculum. While some activities may need to be adapted to take account of learning at home, our curriculum intent and expectations remain consistent.
Independent activities.
Teacher explanations and resources.
Opportunities for feedback and assessment.
Practical, creative and physical activities where appropriate.
Supporting Wellbeing and Screen Time
We recognise that digital learning can increase the amount of time children spend using screens. We encourage children to take regular breaks and include opportunities for reading, physical activity, creativity and other screen-free activities.
The wellbeing of our pupils remains central to our approach, and families are encouraged to contact the school if additional support is needed.
Online Safety and Safeguarding
The safety of our pupils online is extremely important. Children and families are encouraged to follow our online safety guidance and acceptable use expectations.
Our approach to online learning is supported by our:
Data Protection and Security
The school follows data protection requirements, including the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018.
Any information shared through digital platforms will be managed in line with school policies and data protection requirements.
Keeping Devices Secure
Staff and pupils are encouraged to maintain good digital security practices, including:
Through effective use of technology, we aim to support learning, communication and inclusion while ensuring that children remain safe and supported.
Keeping devices and software updated.
Using secure passwords.
Locking devices when not in use.
Monitoring and Supporting Learning at Home
At Lunsford Primary School, we want every child to remain connected to their learning and receive appropriate support when learning takes place away from school.
Monitoring Learning Engagement
Where learning is provided remotely or at home, teachers will monitor children’s engagement and progress through the school’s usual assessment and communication processes.
Teachers will review children’s participation, completion of activities and responses to feedback to ensure that learning remains appropriate and accessible.
Supporting Engagement
We understand that families may experience different circumstances and that children may sometimes need additional support to access learning.
If a child is not engaging with learning, the class teacher will make contact with parents or carers to:
If concerns continue, a member of the school leadership team may contact the family to work together on a plan to support the child’s engagement and wellbeing.
Our aim is to work in partnership with families to ensure that every child feels supported, included and able to continue making progress.
Child Protection and Safeguarding policy
Online safety policy

Acceptable Use Policies
Dear Lunsford Parents and Carers,
We recognise that there may be times when children need to continue their learning away from the classroom. We are committed to working in partnership with families to support children’s learning, wellbeing and progress wherever they are learning.
Our teachers provide learning activities that reflect our curriculum and are designed to help children continue developing their knowledge, skills and confidence. These activities may include a range of resources, including reading, writing, mathematics, creative tasks and opportunities for practical learning.
Learning resources and updates will be shared through the communication platforms used by the school. Families are encouraged to contact their child’s class teacher if they have any questions or need support accessing activities.
We understand that every family’s circumstances are different. While we encourage children to maintain a regular learning routine where possible, we also recognise the importance of balance, wellbeing and family time. Activities such as cooking, gardening, creative projects, playing games and exploring the world around them all provide valuable learning opportunities.
We encourage all children to continue practising key skills regularly, particularly:
Most importantly, we want children to remain curious, confident and engaged in their learning. Thank you for your continued support and partnership.
Kind regards, The Lunsford Primary School Team

Attendance and Absence
Every Day Counts
At Lunsford Primary School, we have high expectations for every child's attendance and punctuality. We expect all pupils to attend school every day and arrive on time unless they are unwell.
Regular attendance is essential to a child's academic achievement, wellbeing, and overall school experience. Children who attend school consistently are more likely to achieve their full potential, develop positive relationships, and benefit from the wide range of opportunities available to them.
As a school, we are committed to promoting excellent attendance and celebrating success. We actively encourage 100% attendance and recognise pupils' commitment through a variety of weekly, termly and annual rewards.
We recognise the vital role that parents and carers play in ensuring good attendance and understand that there may occasionally be challenges that affect a child's ability to attend school. Where concerns arise, we will work in partnership with families and, where appropriate, external agencies to provide support and improve attendance.
Leave of Absence During Term Time
The Department for Education is clear that children should not be taken out of school during term time unless there are exceptional circumstances.
Requests for leave of absence must be made in advance and will only be authorised in exceptional circumstances. Please refer to our Attendance Policy for full details.
Why Attendance Matters
Even a small amount of absence can have a significant impact on a child's learning and progress.
Good attendance helps children to:
Please refer to our Attendance and Punctuality Factsheet to see the impact attendance can have on attainment and educational outcomes.
Achieve their full academic potential
Develop confidence and resilience
Build positive friendships and relationships
Establish good routines and habits
Feel fully included in school life
Reporting an Absence
If your child is unable to attend school for any reason, you must inform the school as soon as possible.
Please telephone the school on:
01732 843352 (Option 1)
The absence line is available 24 hours a day.
Parents and carers are also asked to send a brief note or email when their child returns to school.
Schools are required to account for every half-day absence, so it is important that all absences are reported promptly.
Illness and Returning to School
To help prevent the spread of infection, please follow the guidance below:
Vomiting
Children must remain at home until 24 hours after their last episode of vomiting.
Diarrhoea and Vomiting
Children must remain at home until 48 hours after their last episode of diarrhoea or vomiting.
This helps ensure that any illness has fully cleared before children return to school.
Medical and Dental Appointments
Where possible, medical and dental appointments should be arranged outside school hours.
If your child needs to attend an appointment during the school day:
If your child will miss morning registration and requires a school meal, please ensure the office is informed in advance so that a lunch can be ordered.
Where children leave and return during the school day, a pupil pass will be provided.
First Day Calling
To safeguard all pupils, Lunsford Primary School operates a First Day Calling procedure.
If a child is absent and we have not received notification from a parent or carer, we will contact you to establish the reason for the absence.
If we are unable to make contact and no reason has been provided, the absence will be recorded as unauthorised.
Useful Information and Documents
Please refer to the following documents for further information:
If you have any questions or concerns regarding your child's attendance, please contact the school office. We are always happy to work with families to ensure every child has the best possible opportunity to succeed.

Curriculum
At Lunsford Primary School, we are committed to developing well-rounded, confident and successful learners who are fully prepared for the next stage of their education and equipped to make a positive contribution to society.
Our curriculum has been carefully designed to provide a broad, balanced and ambitious learning experience for every child. Through a rich programme of study, pupils develop key skills, secure knowledge and subject-specific vocabulary that build progressively over time. Learning is carefully sequenced to ensure that children can make meaningful connections, deepen their understanding and apply their knowledge across different contexts.
We make full use of both our indoor and outdoor learning environments, creating engaging opportunities for exploration, discovery and hands-on experiences. Our curriculum is underpinned by our core values and reflects the unique needs, interests and aspirations of our pupils and community.
While our curriculum is firmly rooted in the National Curriculum, we carefully select topics and learning experiences that inspire curiosity, creativity and a lifelong love of learning. Where appropriate, specialist teaching enhances provision and supports children in developing expertise across a range of subjects. We recognise that children learn in different ways and provide varied opportunities to ensure that every learner can experience success.
Sport, the arts and music are an integral part of life at Lunsford. We are passionate about nurturing individual talents and encouraging every child to develop their strengths, interests and confidence.

pageCache.text:
School Clubs and Enrichment Activities including Wrap Around Care
At Lunsford Primary School, we are delighted to offer both Breakfast Club and After School Club provision for our pupils.
Our clubs are delivered by experienced and trained staff who provide high-quality care in a safe, welcoming environment. Children enjoy a healthy range of food options and can take part in a variety of supervised indoor and outdoor activities, helping them to socialise, learn new skills and have fun before and after the school day.
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is hosted at Brookfield Infant School and is available from 7:30am each school day.
Children are provided with a healthy breakfast and can take part in a range of activities before school begins. At 8:30am, a member of the Lunsford Primary School staff team collects the children and safely escorts them to their classrooms.
Booking Information
For further information and to book a place, please visit:
www.flourishfederation.co.uk/breakfast-club-2/
After School Club
Our After School Club is provided by Impact Wrap Around Care and runs from the end of the school day until 6:00pm.
The club offers a safe and enjoyable environment where children can relax, play, take part in activities, and socialise with friends while being cared for by experienced staff.
Booking Information
For further information and to book a place, please visit:
www.impactwraparound.co.uk/about1-c1x1t
Telephone: 07394 651591 Email: impactwraparound@gmail.com
Extra-Curricular Clubs
Lunsford Primary School offers a wide range of extra-curricular clubs throughout the year, providing opportunities for children to develop new skills, pursue their interests and enjoy new experiences.
Most after-school clubs run from 3:10pm until 4:00pm, with children collected from the playground at the end of the session.
Please visit our News and Events section for the latest information about available clubs and activities.
Club Cancellations
Any cancellations or changes to Breakfast Club, After School Club or extra-curricular activities will be communicated to parents and carers as soon as possible.
Please check school communications regularly for updates.

FoLS Meetings, Official Documents & Records
FoLS Committee Meetings are held several times a year. We discuss upcoming events, how we plan to raise additional funds for Lunsford School and projects to assist with improvements to the learning environment. Purchase requests and suggestions are discussed and minutes of our meetings are published below.
The committee meetings are open, meaning anyone can attend. We are all family people, those with young children are very welcome to bring them along.
FoLS Event Meetings are held periodically and are arranged by our Events Coordinator, concentrating on the tasks at had for our upcoming events. We discuss anything from advertising, donation collections, ticket sales to staffing, purchasing of prizes and consumables. Every hand and mind can help, whatever is being planned!

Forest School
Forest School Inspired Learning
As you know our Forest School is evolving and the children will be taking part in Forest School Inspired Learning sessions alongside their class curriculum. Forest School sessions are led by class teachers. The children take part in a number of activities they have access to at Forest School, including using tools, pond dipping, lighting fires, cooking and eating wild food, making dens, taking calculated risks and getting muddy.
How does Forest School Support the Curriculum?
Forest school is a child led kinaesthetic learning experience. The Forest School Team at each session set up a range of activities which are linked to either the topic or a skill area that the class teacher has identified as needing work (such as negotiation, listening skills fine motor skills or management of energy levels). At the beginning of the session the activities are outlined and each child explores these activities throughout the session. The child determines the rate, direction, depth and breadth of their learning. Some activities will lead to unset tasks. The children are encouraged to revisit both skills and projects they have completed in previous weeks to see how time and the environment have had an effect on them and also to ensure that their learning is secure. We encourage exploration of the site at forest school and aim to set up many insect viewing areas. When using natural materials we will always talk about it origins and characteristics. We aim that the children gradually learn the name of the plants up at Forest School and their uses.
Although a kit list is provided for you to support with preparing your child's participation in Forest School, we actively encourage them to begin to learn about weather forecasts and preparing themselves for weather. Even for younger children it is possible for you to have a conversation with your child about what sort of weather we are having and what clothes would be appropriate for them to wear.
Forest School will be delivered on during an afternoon session in the school wood. When your child is scheduled to take part in Forest School we ask that you refer to the kit list suggestions below and ensure that your child is appropriately dressed. Please see note below about the learning opportunity involved in supporting your child to be prepared for Forest School.

Frequently Asked Questions
How is the Forest School project funded?
We have received an increased amount of funding via the PE and Sports Grant to fund improvements to the provision of PE and sport, for the benefit of pupils aged 5-11 years old, so that all pupils develop healthy lifestyles.
So how is Forest School Supporting PE?
The new Curriculum for PE asks schools to provide in both Key Stages “an opportunity for Pupils to develop and master fundamental movement skills, become increasingly competent and confident and access a broad range of opportunities to extend their agility, balance and co-ordination, individually and with others.
They should be able to engage in competitive (both against self and against others) and co-operative physical activities, in a range of increasingly challenging situations.
Pupils should be taught to master basic movements including running, jumping, throwing and catching, as well as developing balance, agility and coordination, and begin to apply these in a range of activities, participate in team games, developing simple tactics for attacking and defending. Apply and develop a broader range of skills, learning how to use them in different ways and to link them to make actions and sequences of movement.
They should enjoy communicating, collaborating and competing with each other. They should develop an understanding of how to improve in different physical activities and learn how to evaluate and recognise their own success. In KS2 they take part in outdoor and adventurous activity challenges both individually and within a team”
At Forest School we play a range of collaborative and individual games which support and develop these physical skills as well as tactics which support team games. We offer tool work which develops both fine and gross motor skills and have a range of physical obstacles which challenge their agility and balance alongside developing risk assessment skills.
We work on core skills such as running and jumping on challenging terrain offering different child specific challenges.
What does my child need to wear for Forest School sessions?
Each term we will provide you with a list of suggested clothing that you child could wear for Forest School sessions. It is important that children begin to learn to plan for different types of weather and also that they recognise when they feel cold or hot. The posters below are suggestions of types of clothing that could be worn in different types of cold temperatures that we may experience during the autumn term.
